{{technical|date=March 2013}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''monopole''' is a [[Connection (fiber bundle)|connection]] over a [[principal bundle]] ''G'' with a section of the associated [[adjoint bundle]].

==Physical interpretation==

Physically, such a monopole can be interpreted in a [[gauge theory]] coupled to a [[Scalar field theory|scalar field]] as a configuration of the scalar and gauge fields which satisfies the [[Bogomolny equations]] and has finite action.  Due to the presence of a scalar field, this monopole is an example of an [['t Hooft–Polyakov monopole]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Katanaev |title=’t Hooft–Polyakov monopoles and a general spherically symmetric solution of the Bogomolny equations |journal=Mod. Phys. Lett. A |date=2023 |volume=38 |doi=10.1142/S0217732323500827}}</ref> and should not be confused with the singular [[magnetic monopoles |monopole solutions]] to Maxwell's equations which are mathematically described by nontrivial principal bundles.
